mark_split.label: Identify a, b, c and find √(a²+b²)

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Identify a, b, c and find √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Compare with a cosx + b sinx + c. There is no constant here, so c = 0 — write it in rather than leaving it out.
lines: Comparing with a cosx + b sinx + c:

accept: compare to get a three b four c zero and root of nine plus sixteen is five
identify the coefficients and take root a squared plus b squared which is five
a is three b is four and the root is five
a three b four c zero, root twenty five equals five
find root a squared plus b squared

steps.why: a cosx + b sinx can always be rewritten as a single sine or cosine of amplitude √(a²+b²). That amplitude is the only thing the max and min depend on.
common_mistakes: Adding a and b instead of their squares.

steps.label: Apply the max and min formulas
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Maximum is c + √(a²+b²) and minimum is c − √(a²+b²). Both are wanted, so give both.

recall.must_convey: That maximum = c + √(a²+b²) = 5 and minimum = c − √(a²+b²) = −5.
accept: maximum is c plus the root which is five and minimum is c minus the root which is minus five
max five and min minus five
apply both formulas to get five and minus five
the two values are five and negative five

steps.why: The expression swings a full amplitude either side of c. With c = 0 the two answers are symmetric about zero.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the c in either formula.
